Working closely with founders and the go-to-market team, you will shape the company's market presence and support inbound growth. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Own external communications across PR, press releases, founder communications, LinkedIn, and the website. - Develop and maintain a consistent brand identity across product, sales materials, social channels, and events. - Plan and deliver the company's presence at industry events, and lead community and partner initiatives. - Grow inbound through content, social, community engagement, and SEO, GEO, and AI search strategies. - Measure channel performance, identify effective approaches, and focus on high-impact initiatives. WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR - Four or more years of experience in B2B marketing, communications, or brand at a startup, scale-up, or agency. - Experience owning external communications and organic growth channels end to end. - Experience organizing or representing a company at industry events. - Fluent German and very good English. - Understanding of SEO, GEO, or AI search, with martech or SaaS experience a plus. - Valid work authorization for Germany, and based in or willing to relocate to Munich. COMPENSATION & BENEFITS Visa sponsorship is not available. A valid work permit for Germany is required. LOCATION On-site in Munich, Bavaria, Germany.

WHAT YOU'LL DO - Design, build, and maintain backend services and APIs for high-throughput workloads. - Identify and resolve performance bottlenecks, from database queries to frontend rendering. - Set up autonomous, scalable workflows that help the product run reliably. - Contribute to frontend and other full-stack work as needed. - Ship product features and improvements quickly, incorporating team feedback. WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR - Two to four years of professional software development experience. - Hands-on experience with Python or Node.js and TypeScript. - Experience with containerization and orchestration tools such as Docker. - Experience building backend services and APIs and optimizing performance across the stack. - A bachelor's or master's degree in computer science or a related field. - Fluent German at C1 level or higher and very good English. - A valid work permit to work in Germany. - A low-ego, ownership-oriented approach to building and improving products. COMPENSATION & BENEFITS Salary range: €80,000 to €110,000 annually. LOCATION On-site in Munich, Bavaria, Germany.

This role requires strong scientific judgment, fluency with the deep learning literature, and the drive to work autonomously in a fast-moving startup environment. WHAT YOU'LL WORK ON - The research literature is vast, rife with ambiguity, and constantly evolving. You'll source, vet, implement, and improve promising ideas from the literature and your own thinking. - Our research is guided by concrete customer needs and product outcomes, not conference benchmarks. You'll have clear context on why your work matters and who it serves. HOW YOU'LL WORK - We believe researchers do their best work with autonomy. You'll have the freedom to pursue problems in the way that works best for you, with the resources and context to back it up. - We expect Research Scientists to collaborate closely with engineers, talk to customers, and shape the product vision. You will bring hands-on experience with scientific or lab automation, and the engineering discipline to make those integrations secure, reliable and scalable across many partners. You will be part of a small team of materials scientists, ML engineers and software engineers, working closely with each other and with our partner labs. You will help define how our AI platform connects to the physical world and shape the tools and practices that link external partner labs to our platform. YOUR IMPACT You will turn experimental labs into first-class, programmable parts of the CuspAI platform. jobs.description_text: THE ROLE We are looking for an ML Engineer* to build, train, and evaluate generative models in our materials discovery platform: diffusion, flow, and autoregressive models that generate material structures according to a prompt of target properties and design constraints. *Note that you would be joining as a ‘Member of Technical Staff’, but the job title above hopefully helps to explain the nature of this role. You will contribute to all aspects of model development: processing training data, defining evals, coming up with hypotheses, implementing models, building training infrastructure, and making sure that the final models are useful in real-world material discovery campaigns. You may be working with inorganic crystals, molecules, polymers, metal-organic compounds, and other material classes. You will be part of a small dedicated team, but interact with a large group of chemists, machine learning research, and engineers. YOUR IMPACT In this role you will be building novel generative models that transform how we design new materials, which is critical for accelerating the discovery of next-generation materials for energy and sustainability challenges. The models you will build will be used to design materials for better solar cells, catalysts, semiconductors, batteries, carbon-capture sorbents, and so on. jobs.title: Software Engineer, C++ (Onboard Platform)
jobs.description_text: This in-office expectation does not apply to contractor positions ABOUT THE ROLE Applied Intuition is building Level 4 autonomous technology for vehicles deployed around the world. The reliability of the L4 system is a key element for our autonomy program, and a must-have to safely enable driverless operations on public roads. In the rare case where the system has a hardware or software problem, it needs to be able to detect it and safely bring the vehicle to a safe state if that happens. To achieve this level of reliability and safety, every component of the stack needs to be built to meet the highest quality bar, and that is especially true for the platform layer at the base of the entire system. Our team builds the foundation of the Level 4 stack, starting with autonomous trucks. We sit between the autonomy algorithms and the vehicle, and we work with every team in the program to take the fleet from supervised testing to driverless operation. Your work will run on real trucks on public roads, and it will be measured by how far the fleet drives between failures. We crawl the web continuously and cannot keep all of it, refresh all of it, or spend a GPU on all of it. Something has to decide which pages are worth indexing, which links are worth following, which pages say the same thing as pages we already have, what has gone stale, and what we should never have picked up. Today they run on a mix of learned signals and thresholds someone picked. We are looking for a research engineer to own the signals behind those decisions, and the decisions themselves. jobs.description_text: JOB SUMMARY Every Etched system starts its life in a lab. Before a rack-scale inference product reaches a customer, it goes through bring-up, validation, and testing in our factories, labs, or data centers, and each of those environments needs networked, provisioned, monitored infrastructure that is ready before the hardware arrives. The Infra Labs team builds and runs that infrastructure. As an Infrastructure Engineer on Infra Labs, you will own the racks and server infrastructure across Etched's labs and data center sites, from our office lab at Santana Row to our new hardware facility in Milpitas and our Bay Area colocation footprint. Once our forward-deployed engineers physically install a system, you take it from there: getting it onto the network, provisioned, connected to the storage and compute services it depends on, observable, and healthy through bring-up and testing. jobs.title: Senior Research Scientist - AI Safety
jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE TEAM We are the central research and development team driving Faculty's broader AI safety charter. We pioneer fundamental and applied technical AI safety research, producing rigorous scientific outputs—including publications, tooling, and technical reports—that advance the theory and practice of AI safety and directly shape the work of frontier AI labs, government agencies, and national security institutes. Our research spans both black-box and white-box approaches to understanding and steering AI systems. We care deeply about interpretability, faithfulness, and principled mitigation strategies, with a particular focus on the mechanistic and behavioural study of transformer-based large language models and long-running agentic systems. We operate at the cutting edge of the field, with current research threads including: - System Understanding: Interpretability, steering vectors, and the science of evaluations. - Control & Alignment: Goal drift, machine unlearning, and uncertainty calibration. - Societal Safeguards: Misinformation mitigation and robust deployment boundaries. We collaborate closely with the Faculty's wider AI safety team, a group with a well-established track record in capability evaluations and red-teaming for misuse risk across CBRN, cybersecurity, and international security. jobs.title: Senior Product Designer
jobs.description_text: ABOUT FRONTIER Faculty Frontier™ is a decision operating system. It puts AI to work on the decisions that matter most to large organisations, such as where to invest, how to allocate resources, and when to act. Every enterprise is investing heavily in AI, but few are confident it will improve performance. Too often it goes to what’s easy to automate, disconnected from the decisions that actually move the business. Frontier works backwards from objectives like revenue, margin and risk to the decisions that drive them, then connects the data, models and agents those decisions need into a world model of the business. Teams simulate and optimise options with ADA, our AI decision agent, and every decision is tracked against its outcome so the system keeps learning. Our ambition is to make business decisions as easy to navigate as getting around a city. We don’t believe in AI that thinks for people. We believe in AI that helps people think, with humans and agents working together inside a decision system. Customers start with one high-value decision and prove value in weeks. Over months they connect it into a wider decision network, and over years they build an adaptive enterprise. Frontier is built by Faculty, an AI company that has delivered more than 400 systems since 2014 and is now part of Accenture. jobs.title: Member of Technical Staff – Infrastructure
jobs.description_text: THE ROLE We train action policies and world models on the largest corpus of action-labeled gaming data in the world, and we run Medal, a platform used by millions of gamers every day. Both depend on the same infrastructure: billions of gameplay clips a year that have to be stored, moved and served, under research workloads one day and consumer traffic the next. We're looking for a generalist infra engineer to own that end to end, with cloud and storage at the center: the cloud architecture and the fleet it runs on, object storage for petabytes of gameplay video, and the data pipelines and CI/CD around them. You'll make the architecture calls before scale turns them into emergencies, plan for where today's systems break at 10x the data, traffic or team, and go from infra design straight into application code when that's what the problem needs. You'll also build our infrastructure function in New York: set the technical direction, hire and grow the team, and define how we design, review, deploy and run systems, while staying hands-on yourself. You'll work directly with research and product engineering across General Intuition and Medal, and be the person they pull in for system design. WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR - Deep, hands-on cloud and storage experience, run in production. We run on GCP and CoreWeave; what matters is that you've owned Terraform, IAM and Kubernetes on a major cloud, and object storage at a scale where placement, tiering and egress cost were your decisions. - 6+

jobs.title: Member of Technical Staff – Simulation
jobs.description_text: THE ROLE We train models on games that act across many embodiments, and simulation is a growing part of how we extend them. In this role, you'll push in two directions: going deeper into control, by training low-level controllers for our robots with RL in sim, and going wider, by building environments realistic enough to train in, not just to evaluate. You'll own both, from the physics up to how the controllers plug into our models. This is an in-person role based in one of our New York, Geneva, or Zurich offices. WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR - Deep, hands-on simulation experience, run in production. We run on Isaac Sim and MuJoCo; what matters is that you've owned environments, assets and domain randomization in a major simulator, and physics at a fidelity where contact models, actuator dynamics and solver settings were your decisions. - 6+ years of hands-on exposure to robot learning in simulation (contact-rich manipulation, legged locomotion, whole-body control, or similar), with strong fundamentals in reinforcement learning, and sim-to-real transfer. - Proven ability to bridge simulation and real-world robotic systems.
